title: SDK snapshot fidelity layers and tool delegation notes
content:
Purpose
-----
This doc collects product- and SDK-facing notes for an incremental delivery model I’m calling "snapshot fidelity layers". The core idea: return the most useful, typed partial state (a snapshot) at several fidelity levels during streaming responses so clients can safely act (call tools, show intermediate UI, do progressive rendering) without needing to parse an arbitrary token stream.

Why this is different / why we need it
----------------------------------
- Many of our existing streaming PRDs assume purely token deltas or partial JSON fragments. That leaves clients to implement expensive, brittle parsers and makes tool-calling fragile when an intermediate partial JSON is invalid.
- Product teams want deterministic checkpoints they can use to call third‑party APIs, store intermediate transcripts, or show a consistent UI snapshot even if the completion later changes.
- SDK ergonomics must make it easy to consume snapshots without forcing a ton of ad-hoc reconcilers in app code.

Goals (what success looks like)
-----------------------------
1) Provide 2–4 lightweight snapshot fidelity levels emitted during a single streaming call (minimal, structured-core, enriched, final).
2) Guarantee that each snapshot is a self-contained JSON object (typed) clients can deserialize and act upon.
3) Define minimal SDK primitives (JS + Python) that wire into existing streaming endpoints and expose: a snapshot event handler, a tool-delegation helper, resume semantics, and backpressure signals.
4) Keep byte overhead low: delta token payloads still flow, but snapshots are emitted as compact typed frames only when necessary (configurable by policy).

High‑level design
-----------------
- Frames: every streaming response is a sequence of frames. There are two orthogonal axes: payload type (token_delta | snapshot) and fidelity tag (f0|min, f1|structured, f2|enriched, fX|final). Each frame has a monotonic frame_id, monotonic snapshot_version when applicable, and optional parent_snapshot_id for branching sessions (client-side branching).
- Snapshot invariant: any snapshot frame MUST be valid JSON conforming to a lightweight schema for that model+prompt. Schema is loosely typed (map of known keys), but must parse without requiring incremental string repair.
- Tool delegation markers: snapshots include an optional tools[] array of intent objects (tool id, confidence, args schema). SDK helpers convert these into idempotent tool invocation packages with retry semantics and structured results insertion.
- Resume and rehydration: snapshots are checkpointed as concise diffs against the previous snapshot_version. Clients can request a resumed stream from a given snapshot_version and the server will replay token_deltas from after that checkpoint or re-emit the stable snapshot if needed.

Example minimal snapshot frame (textual example)
------------------------------------------------
{
  "frame_id": "f-000123",
  "type": "snapshot",
  "fidelity": "structured",
  "snapshot_version": "v3",
  "timestamp": "2025-02-12T15:04:10Z",
  "body": {
    "summary": "Plan: three bullets",
    "actions": [
      {"tool": "search", "query": "pricing API"},
      {"tool": "http_post", "url": "https://example.com/notify", "payload_preview": {"title":"Draft"}}
    ],
    "sources": ["url://x", "url://y"]
  }
}

Note: the above is an emitted snapshot and therefore MUST be syntactically valid JSON. Token deltas that follow may still refine the text but the snapshot represents a safe, callable state.

SDK ergonomics (JS sketch)
-------------------------
API surface (proposal):
- client.streamWithSnapshots(opts) -> returns AsyncIterable of frames
- onSnapshot(frame, helpers) -> helper methods: helpers.invokeTool(toolSpec), helpers.commitCheckpoint(), helpers.applyPatch(patch)

Usage sketch:

const it = client.streamWithSnapshots({model, prompt, snapshotPolicy: 'structured|every-400ms'});
for await (const frame of it) {
  if (frame.type === 'snapshot') {
    ui.renderStable(frame.body);
    // safe to call external system based on declared tools
    if (frame.body.actions) {
      await helpers.invokeTool(frame.body.actions[0]); // idempotent wrapper + retry
      helpers.commitCheckpoint(frame.snapshot_version);
    }
  } else if (frame.type === 'token_delta') {
    ui.append(frame.text);
  }
}

Key SDK ergonomics decisions
---------------------------
- Expose both raw frame stream and higher-level convenience event hooks. Some apps will need raw tokens; others will prefer snapshot-driven flows.
- helpers.invokeTool() will be opinionated: it wraps network retry, idempotency keys derived from frame_id+tool index, and automatic result insertion back into a stable checkpoint object (so subsequent snapshots show the tool result).
- Provide combinators: mapSnapshots(fn), throttleSnapshots(ms), dedupeSnapshotVersions(), and a small stateful "reconciler" primitive that merges snapshot.body into client state using a declared schema.

Bandwidth and SLO considerations
-------------------------------
- Policy: snapshots are only emitted when the model reaches a stable extraction for that fidelity or when an explicit time threshold elapses. Default: structured snapshot every 400ms up to 3 times, enriched once near the end. This keeps snapshot overhead below ~5–8% token bandwidth for typical prompts.
- Server should support snapshot suppression for constrained customers (non-snapshot mode).

Telemetry + observability
------------------------
Important fields to emit in tracing/metrics:
- snapshot_emitted (bool), snapshot_fidelity, snapshot_size_bytes, time_to_first_snapshot_ms, time_between_snapshots_ms, invoked_tool_count, tool_invoke_latency_ms, resume_requests_from_snapshot_version.
- Surface rate of failed snapshot deserializations (should be zero if invariant kept).

Backward compatibility & migration path
--------------------------------------
- Old streaming clients continue to receive token_delta frames unchanged. New snapshot frames are additive and will be ignored by naïve token consumers.
- SDKs provide a compatibility shim: if client opts into snapshotPolicy, server begins emitting snapshot frames on existing endpoints. No new endpoint is required.

Failure modes and mitigation
---------------------------
- Snapshot emitted but tool invocation fails -> helpers expose structured error and can attach a recovery action; server may re-emit a corrective snapshot after the model re-generates with tool outputs.
- Snapshot schema drift between model versions -> include a model_version field on snapshots and a compatibility hint; default to safe keys (summary, actions, sources).
- Network partitions during resume -> server returns a resume token and a hint to re-request final snapshot when available.

Open questions / tradeoffs
-------------------------
- How large can snapshots be before they defeat their purpose? (target: < 4KB typical).
- Should tools[] include explicit cost/risk metadata so SDKs can prompt user confirmation before invoking high-risk tools?
- Do we need a separate authorization scope for tool invocations originating from snapshots (enterprise security)?
- How to model branching: user edits previous prompt during a long session — do we treat subsequent snapshots as children or as replacing the linear version?

Next steps (short roadmap)
-------------------------
- Proto API review with backend runtime team (Marco) — define minimal frame wire format and sequence guarantees (2 weeks).
- Build JS SDK prototype with: AsyncIterable frames, helpers.invokeTool, reconciler primitive (4 weeks).
- Telemetry schema and tracing hooks (Sofia + SRE) — add spans and metrics (2 weeks).
- Internal playbook: instrument a small internal app (examples/team-collab) and run 2 week trial to measure bandwidth + tool reliability.

Notes to self
-------------
- Keep snapshots as single JSON objects. Avoid partial/fragmented JSON in frames.
- We must make idempotency implicit and automatic for tool invocations to avoid user errors.
- Prepare a simple migration doc for customer-facing SDK changes (small code diff).

Appendix: quick wire-format idea (line-delimited JSON over SSE)
------------------------------------------------------------
- frame-type: json object string, preceded by a short header: "FRAME <len>\n" then the JSON payload. Easier for servers to batch and for clients to fast-fail if header mismatch.
- Alternative: a small binary envelope (proto) — more efficient but slower to iterate in SDKs.

End of draft.

(leave TODO markers where appropriate, collect feedback from runtime team before locking schema)
